claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'd like to check if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! It's lovely to meet you, and I'll help you work out if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me start with a few questions:

How old is Alex?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 17, I need to ask a follow-up question:

Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar), or on an approved training course?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. That's an important detail.

Just to confirm, is Alex currently employed or looking for work, or is there another reason he's not in education or training at the moment? Also, has he recently left education (within the past 20 weeks)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's working - he has a full-time job at the supermarket.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a couple more questions to make sure I have the full picture:

1. Are you responsible for Alex (i.e., does he live with you, or do you contribute towards his upkeep)?

2. Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives with me here at home, and yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Based on the information you've provided, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me provide you with my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**For Alex (age 17):**
Child Benefit can be claimed for children until they turn 16, or until they turn 20 if they stay in approved full-time education or training. Since Alex is 17 and is working full-time rather than being in qualifying education or training, he no longer meets the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

If Alex's circumstances were to change in the future—for example, if he decided to return to full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels or an equivalent qualification)—you may become eligible again at that point.

I hope this helps clarify things. Is there anything else you'd like to know?

Child Benefit can only be claimed for a child aged 16-19 if they remain in qualifying full-time education or approved training. Since Alex is neither in education nor training, and is instead employed, the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit are not met.
